served.stem: Chytrids (phylum Chytridiomycota) are set apart from all other fungi by which feature?
choices: Cell walls built from cellulose instead of chitin
served.bankWhy: This question is pointing at the one fungal lineage that kept a swimming stage. Chytrids release zoospores that each carry a single posterior flagellum, something no other fungal group does, and it suits their life in water and saturated soil. Anchor it to the sound of the name: chytrids swim.

choiceTexts: Cell walls built from cellulose instead of chitin

answer.line: Chytrids are the only fungi that kept a swimming stage: spores that each carry one flagellum.

steps: List what every fungus shares first: chitin walls, food absorbed from outside, reproduction by spores.
Cross off anything true of fungi in general. A shared trait cannot set one group apart.
What is left is the swimming spore. Chytrids make zoospores with one tail; every other fungus lost the flagellum.

choices.note: Zoospores with a single flagellum. No other fungus swims.
No fungus photosynthesizes. Every fungus, chytrids included, absorbs food it digested outside its body.

choices.text: Cell walls built from cellulose instead of chitin
choices.note: Cellulose walls belong to plants and to the fungus-like water molds. Chytrid walls are chitin, like every other fungus.
Most chytrids are single cells or simple threads. Big multicellular bodies belong to the molds and mushrooms.
Chytrids reproduce both sexually and asexually. Asexual only was the old catch-all for fungi with no known sexual stage.
